summary.systemic_finding: narrative_neutral is the dominant failure mode: 22/26 F_narrative fields state the entrustment relationship (el0) and, for ipc405_use_or_disposal, frequently also the governing contract/direction (el2) as scene-setting, before the element facts restate the same content. Only records that keep the narrative anonymous ('an individual', 'staff members', 'the coordinator' with no stated custodial relationship) pass — these are exactly the omit:0 misappropriation records (0000, 0005, 0010, 0015), where the teacher evidently was careful not to leak the specific omitted element but did not apply the same care to keeping narratives neutral generally. Every ipc405_use_or_disposal record fails narrative_neutral, and two of its control records (0007, 0008) have the narrative reciting all three required elements in full, making the element facts almost redundant restatements. Separately, character-name and setting templates repeat closely across contracts ('Elias Thorne' custodian-of-an-archive-with-audit-discrepancies in both t_ipc405_misappropriation_r1_0013 and t_ipc405_wilfully_suffers_r1_0002; 'Priya Sharma, estate executor' in both t_ipc405_use_or_disposal_r1_0003 and 0007; the informal village-festival entrustment template in t_ipc405_misappropriation_r1_0002 and 0012), and a generic 'logistics coordinator manages a warehouse' skeleton recurs across at least five records spanning all three contracts.
